The Tools group is the way in. Three rows: the conversation, the connection, and the calls. Two of them open pages of their own, one each.

Row Command What it does
Open the AI panel temcoAi.openPanel Reveals the conversation; the same row puts it away. A plain open toggles, because the row a reader opens a thing with is the row they reach for again. A caller that names a page never closes anything
The Tool Server temcoAi.connection The program behind every call: whether it is running, where it answers, how to stop it, and the two settings it reads
The tools it can call temcoAi.tools The catalogue itself

The title bar carries the same two ideas as buttons, so the group is useful without opening a page. The log is not a fourth row: it is a button on the Tool Server page, where the rest of the program's state is.

Two pages rather than one, because a status and a list are different questions and the first one is asked when something is wrong. A page that answered both put a Start button under a catalogue that had to be loaded before the button could be seen — which is exactly the state (nothing is running) in which the catalogue cannot load.

temcoAi.tools is a page, not a tree view, because a flat list of rows cannot show an argument schema. Two parts:

  • The catalogue: tabs, one per part of the API, taken from the first word of each call's name and kept in the order the server lists them, with a count beside each: Device 8, Docs 4, Repo 5. The strip is a plain row of words with their counts: twelve-pixel labels in the section's own face at six hundred weight, the first letter capitalised, no background under the pointer or under the open tab, and a single hairline in the theme's primary colour along the bottom of the tab that is open. The strip wraps rather than scrolling, so no tab is ever hidden past its right edge. The calls of the open tab run across the row as cells: device.list over Every T3000 device…, device.describe over One device in full…, as many per row as fit, each description cut to three lines with the whole sentence on hover, so one long sentence cannot set the height of every row. The name and its sentence share one face — a name in monospace read as code, and these are not code. The name is a link that selects that call in the runner, seeds its arguments and scrolls there, which is the only thing a reader clicking a name could have wanted. The open tab shows six cells and carries the way to the rest at the right end of the strip: Show 2 more, which names what is held back, and Show less once it is out. There is no reads-and-writes split; the calls that stop for a person are named in one line under the strip instead of being a heading. Fetched through tools/list when the page opens — which starts the server if it is not up — so the list cannot drift from what the model is offered.
  • Run one: the picker the links drive, the arguments as JSON seeded from the chosen tool's schema, and the answer. It calls the same callTool() the loop uses, so a write still asks the person first: the page is a second way in to the same gate, not around it.

When the catalogue cannot be read, the page says why and offers the Tool Server page rather than an install button: the reason is almost always that nothing is running, and starting it is a decision that belongs where its state is shown.

temcoAi.connection is the other half:

  • Status: a word with a dot beside it — Running, Starting, Failed, Stopped — then the address it answers on (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp), how many tools it offers, its process id, and how long it has been up. Under them Start, Stop, Restart, and Show the log. The buttons disable themselves while a start is in flight and when they are the wrong verb for the state, so nothing offers "Stop" to something that is not running.
  • The program: installed or not, where, the platform, and the artifact id — with the dotnet publish line when there is nothing installed, because a source checkout is the case that has no release to download from.

Both Where it answers and Platform API were removed from this page, and each for the same reason: a page about one program should describe that program, not ask the reader to configure something they cannot yet use.

Removed Why it was there Where it lives now
Port field A fixed port is only needed by something outside this window that has to reach a known address — an inspector, a script. Everyone else gets a free port per start, which is what stops two windows colliding temcoAi.serverPort, in Settings. The address it produces is still shown, read-only, in Status
Platform API field It names the HTTP service the device, repository and project tools ask. No such service exists yet (open decision 1), so the field asked a person to configure an address that could not answer temcoAi.platformApi, in Settings; the Temco AI: Platform API command now opens the setting instead of a page

Four things the page does not do, each a decision:

  1. Nothing starts on open. A status page that changes what it reports is not a status page.
  2. Nothing is guessed. A stop and a crash both end in a process that is gone; only the exit itself separates them, which is why the failure branch carries the last lines the process wrote.
  3. The log is a button, not a row. It is a page about one program, and the log is one of the things that program produces.
  4. The state is repainted from the module, not re-rendered. Start, stop and restart each answer with a status message that the page's own script paints into the four facts it owns, so a field halfway through being typed is never thrown away.

Three older dialogs were removed in favour of these pages: a status toast that said only that the server was ready, an input box that asked for an address without saying what it was for, and a row that opened a page with no status on it.

10. Security#

Concern Rule
The model decides what to call The loop is the boundary, not the model's goodwill: DESTRUCTIVE is a set in the extension, not a property read from the server
A write reaches equipment Only after an explicit yes in the panel, and the yes is recorded with the arguments
The server is reachable from the network It is not: the socket is bound to 127.0.0.1 by name, never 0.0.0.0
Another process on this machine calls it Every request but /health needs the bearer token this window generated at start. The token lives in memory, is passed in the child's environment rather than its arguments, and dies with the process
The catalog is modified Opened ReadOnly (§5.6); writes stay in temco-store
A tool result is code Results are text and are rendered as text, never evaluated
A downloaded server is tampered with Pinned sha256 per platform where the catalogue has one; where it does not, the download is confirmed once with the file's origin and size in front of the person, and the checksum it had is recorded
Secrets None are passed but the per-start token; the environment is a curated list, not a copy of the host's

11. Decisions#

Settled, with the reason each one was settled that way:

  1. The server is HTTP, and the window manages it. TEMCO_MCP_TRANSPORT=http is what the application starts, on loopback, with a per-start token. The reason is not throughput: a pipe has no address and no state, so a page could only ever say "ready" or nothing. A program that writes needs a stop button, and a stop button needs a process someone owns. stdio stays as the second mode, because it is what an inspector and a script want, and it is one switch in Program.cs.
  2. The server is downloaded, not bundled. 108 MB and 344 files per platform in every installer is worse than a verified download on first use through the machinery that already installs models. A release attaches temco-mcp-<rid>.tar.gz for each of its three platforms, and the catalogue asks for the one that matches the running application's version. Bundling stays available for an air-gapped build by adding the artifact to the catalogue with a file:// URL.
  3. Two pages, not one. The catalogue and the connection were one page for a while. They are two questions asked at different times, and the state in which the catalogue cannot be read is the state in which the connection is the only thing worth showing.
  4. The log is a button on the Tool Server page, not a row in the panel. The panel names things a person goes to; a log is what a person goes to after something on a page has gone wrong.
  5. The supervisor starts the server, not the loop. runAgent used to own the process because it was the only consumer. It has three now — the loop, the runner, the catalogue — and the page that shows the address has to be looking at the process the others use.
  6. A missing checksum is a question, not a refusal. The entry used to demand a setting be found before the first download, which made "Start" a dead end on a machine that had never enabled it. The confirmation carries more information than the setting ever did — the exact URL, the size, the destination — and the observed checksum is recorded either way, so nothing is lost by asking instead of refusing. Pinning the hashes stays the goal; it is a data task that needs one build to exist first, and allowUnpinned now means only "do not ask".

Still open:

  1. Who answers TEMCO_PLATFORM_API. The device, repo, and project tools need one HTTP surface. Either a service in the product answers it, or IPlatformApi gains an implementation that speaks T3000 protocols directly and the URL becomes a connection setting. Only HttpPlatformApi changes either way.
  2. Where the audit lives. The server owns audit.db in this document, while the extension already owns the store schema. One has to be authoritative before the first release.
  3. Whether the 7B model may act by default. The 1.5B model may not; the catalogue can carry a per-model maxTools and a mayCallDestructive flag.
  4. Whether one process should serve several windows. The token is per window and the port is per window, so two windows run two processes. A shared process would need a shared token and a supervisor outside the extension host; nothing needs it yet.
  5. Whether /health should need the token. It does not, so the supervisor can poll it before it knows anything. It exposes the name and version of a program whose binary is on the same disk.

12. Where the code is#

design/authoring-and-msdn-output.title: Authoring parity with Dr.Explain, publishing parity with MSDN
design/authoring-and-msdn-output.html:
The product direction is two references at once, and they answer different questions:

  • Dr.Explain is the authoring reference: how a person starts a project, brings existing material in, and edits topics with their properties in front of them.
  • MSDN is the output reference: what a reader gets. The website is the product; CHM and PDF are the same tree in other clothes.

Where the two disagree, MSDN wins — a surface that looks like Dr.Explain but does not produce an MSDN-shaped site has failed the requirement.

1. Where we stand today#

Everything below is what the code does, not what the mock draws.

Thing Where Reality today
A project catalog documents row (extensions/temco-store/src/catalog/schema.ts) name, slug, version, audience, owner, timestamps
What it reads doc_sources (many-to-many, per-source branch + include glob) created by the wizard's Sources step
What it builds recipes (engine, config_path, script, outputs) the wizard writes engine: 'docfx' and the ticked outputs
Outputs offered extensions/temco-projects/src/projectFlow.ts website · PDF · offline help (CHM) · search index · AI index
Creation flow src/projectFlow.ts 4 steps: Basics (name, version, owner, audience) → Sources → Outputs → Review
Content each product repository's docs/help/registry.json + Markdown (extensions/temco-docs/src/registry.ts) the repository is the source of truth; the platform reads it
Page metadata already modelled RegistryPage title, area, chapter, order, audience, ship, owner, tags, keywords, help_ids, code, reviewed
Authoring already implemented newPagePage.ts (3-step new page), pageOps.ts (writePage — the only disk write), registryEdit.ts (field writes) a page is created from the location + template + draft, and registry fields survive regeneration
Builds extensions/temco-docs/src/builds.ts the repository's own scripts (docs:site, docs:build, build:help:dry) run as VS Code tasks, and success is judged by the artifacts
Checks diagnostics.ts, sections.ts structure, staleness, unreviewed pages

Two consequences worth stating plainly:

  1. We already have the Dr.Explain page properties. ship is its "export conditions", help_ids is its "help context ID", keywords is its index, order is its TOC position, and owner/audience/reviewed are its bookkeeping. Nothing in the data model is missing for authoring.
  2. We are missing the front door and the import. Creation starts at "name, version, owner" — a project is assumed to have content already. There is no way to begin from a Word file, an HTML folder, a CHM, a template, or a repository.

2. Dr.Explain's flow, from the surfaces#

Start page:

  • four ways in — Create a local project, Create a shared project on the server, Checkout project from the server, Open an existing project;
  • six importers — Microsoft Word, RTF, Compiled HTML Help (CHM), HLP, Standalone HTML, folder of HTML/TXT/XML;
  • recent projects and templates in all languages.

Editor:

  • topic tree with a synthetic Title / Table of contents root and numbered topics;
  • properties panel per topic: title, filename, export conditions, status, header/footer, page numbering, help context IDs;
  • central page with Menu / Index / Search tabs;
  • toolbar previews: Content editor, HTML preview, CHM preview, PDF preview;
  • AI assistant rail with the model/provider setting.

3. Gap analysis#

Capability Dr.Explain Us today What it means
Start from nothing local project have it (Basics step) —
Start from a template templates in all languages no a template is a repository-shaped skeleton; cheap and high value
Start from existing material Word, RTF, CHM, HLP, HTML, folder a folder the platform can already read is now adoptable (temcoProjects.discover); Word, RTF, CHM, HLP and loose HTML are still not still the biggest gap, and smaller by one case
Shared / checkout server + checkout git remote + clone exists in temco-repositories, not in the project flow map to git, do not build a server
Topic tree editing drag, renumber, nest tree view + order field add reorder → order write
Per-topic properties full panel registry fields, but no form form over registryEdit
Export conditions per topic ship expose it
Context IDs / index per topic help_ids, keywords expose them
WYSIWYG body editing HTML editor inside the tool Markdown in the editor + rendered preview do not copy; MSDN topics are Markdown
Preview before build HTML · CHM · PDF HTML preview exists; CHM/PDF only after a build add CHM/PDF preview after first build
MSDN-shaped site — the site is the repository generator's; our output choice is website make the contract explicit (§5)

4. Decisions#

D1 — Creation asks where the content comes from, not a cosmetic "type". The origin decides which steps follow and what gets written on Create. A dropdown that changes nothing is worse than none.

Origin What it does on Create Writes
Blank project creates the project; the first page is authored here documents + recipes
From template copies a template folder into the chosen location, then the project cites it template tree + documents + doc_sources
From a repository (Dr.Explain's "shared") clones/attaches a remote at a branch and reads its docs/help/registry.json sources + doc_sources
Import a document set converts the material into pages, then the project cites the folder Markdown tree + registry entries + doc_sources
Open existing picks a folder that already holds a registry sources only

D2 — Importers write the repository's contract, never a second content store. An importer is a converter: source → docs/help/*.md + docs/help/registry.json, exactly the shape the product's own generator writes. The platform database stays what it is (a register of projects, sources, builds, releases) — otherwise the same text would live twice and drift.

D3 — MSDN is an output contract, not a theme. See §5.

D4 — Page properties are ours already; add only what MSDN needs. Expose ship, order, keywords, help_ids, audience, owner through a form in the page editor. Two new optional fields are worth having: kind (concept · how-to · reference · tutorial — MSDN's ms.topic) and applies_to (the product versions a page is for). Header/footer and page numbering are template settings for PDF, not per page.

D5 — Collaboration is git, not a server. "Shared project" = a project whose source is a repository with a remote; "checkout" = clone + branch; review is a pull request. temco-repositories already clones, pulls and records branches. Building a Dr.Explain server would duplicate what the repository host already does better.

D6 — The website is the product; CHM and PDF derive from it. One tree, three targets: website (primary), CHM (same topics, help_ids → HH context IDs, keywords → index), PDF (one print profile).

5. The MSDN contract (what "similar to MSDN" means concretely)#

Structure. area → chapter → topic, the shape the registry already has. A topic is one Markdown file; order decides TOC position; a page not in the registry is not published.

URL. /{area}/{chapter}/{slug} — stable, lowercase, no build hash. Renaming a slug writes a redirect entry, because links outlive builds.

Every topic page carries:

  • breadcrumb Area / Chapter / Title;
  • left TOC of the whole set with the current branch open;
  • an on-page TOC built from ##/###;
  • Applies to (from applies_to, or the project version);
  • previous / next in TOC order;
  • feedback and a "this page is stale" signal from reviewed;
  • a permalink for every heading.

Index and search. keywords feeds the site index; the search index (already a wizard target) is built from titles, headings and keywords, so a reader can reach a page by a controller's name as well as by its title.

Version selector. A released version is a releases row; the site serves the newest plus archived versions. The version selector is a list of those rows, not a rebuild.

CHM. The same tree compiled with help_ids as context IDs, keywords as the index, and the chapters as the TOC levels. A topic that is ship: false is in the site's draft preview and not in the CHM.

Where the furniture is produced — and why Temco Learn is not it. A topic page is rendered by the product repository's own site generator (docs:site), and Learn's Article Preview opens the published file rather than drawing a second copy of it (extensions/temco-workbench/src/learnPages.ts: “a preview that can disagree with the shipped page is worse than no preview”). So the platform's half of the contract is the metadata that makes the furniture possible — order for the TOC, keywords for the index, ship for what is published, help_ids for the CHM, title for the heading and the breadcrumb — and the generator's half is drawing it. Adding a page-properties form (phase 2, below) is what closes the loop between them.

6. The project flow, redesigned#

Five steps; step 2–4 are the steps we have, unchanged in content.

  1. Origin — Blank · Template · Repository · Import · Open existing.
  2. Basics — name, version, owner, audience (today's step 1).
  3. Bring in — shape follows the origin: template picker · repository picker (remote + branch) · importer picker (Word/RTF/HTML/HTML folder/CHM) with a destination folder · folder picker.
  4. What it builds — the targets we already offer, with Website ticked for a new project.
  5. Review — what will be written, and where the files land. Nothing is written before this step.

Two rules stay: nothing is written until the last button, and the project you create becomes the selected project.

7. Phases#

Phase Deliverable Status
1 documents.origin + documents.template (schema 4, with a migration); wizard step Origin (blank · repository · folder · template · import), where the origin decides what the third step asks; a template writes a starter docs/help tree and refuses to overwrite anything; folder and template projects record their folder as a source done
2 Page-properties form (temcoDocs.pageProperties, Markdown title-bar action) over registryEdit: title, owner, audience, order, ships, keywords, tags, help_ids, with the confirmation naming every value it will write done
3 Importers (temcoDocs.import, called by the wizard's Import a document set origin): HTML folder / page and Markdown folder natively; Word / RTF / ODT through pandoc; CHM through hh.exe -decompile (Windows). All four write the repository contract and refuse a folder that already has a registry done
4 The platform's half of the MSDN contract: the metadata itself (title, order, keywords, ship, help_ids, audience), which phase 2 made editable and which the module's existing validation already reports on. A separate readiness page was built and then removed: it re-tested the same fields without adding a decision, and the Pipeline group already has Review Center and Build Center. The drawing half — breadcrumb, on-page TOC, prev/next, permalinks, redirects, version selector — belongs to each product repository's docs:site generator, which is not in this repository platform half done
5 CHM/PDF previews after a build (temcoDocs.openArtifact, from the Build Center's artifact rows); drag reorder → order (already in pageOps.handleDrop); the repository origin cites recorded sources and links to the Sources page, where temcoRepositories.fetchSource clones done

Phase 1 is the answer to "do we add more types?" — yes, five origins, and each one changes what the next step asks.

8. What we deliberately do not copy#

  • Its WYSIWYG HTML editor. MSDN topics are Markdown; the editor is VS Code's, and the page renders beside it.
  • Its project database. The repository keeps the text; the platform keeps the register.
  • Its server and checkout. Git and pull requests.
  • Its single-file exports as the main path. The site is the product; CHM is one of its outputs.

design/t3000-support-engineering.title: Support intake — engineering
design/t3000-support-engineering.html:
How the support window in t3000-support-intake.md is actually built: the stack, the contract between the two processes, and the method for each part. The intake document decides what exists; this one decides how.

Every technology named here is already in the repository it belongs to. Nothing new is added to any of the three products except source files.

1. The stack at a glance#

Layer Language Runtime and libraries already present What it owns
T3000 shell C++14 (MFC) CMake, CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 14, WebView2 1.0.1150.38 (x86), jsoncpp (Json-cpp/include), GDI+ (mygdiplus.h) capture, context, logs, outbox, handoff, crash marker
T3000 web UI TypeScript 5.8, React 18.3 Vite under Quasar 2, React Router 6.22, Fluent UI v9 (@fluentui/react-components), Vitest the Support page: four steps, annotation, Help & Learn
T3000 local service Rust axum 0.7, tokio, tokio-tungstenite, rusqlite — HTTP on 9103, WebSocket on 9104 serves the bundle; already the localhost origin the window is loaded from
Temco Platform TypeScript VS Code workbench fork, the src/temco shell (43 KB), temco-* extensions with webview panels the inbox, the issue draft, the forum draft
Temco Learn Markdown, DocFX the site's own generator the forum topic, after approval
Automation YAML + shell GitHub Actions, GITHUB_TOKEN only labels, dedupe, one comment, the docs-owed flag

Three languages, and each is already the language of the thing it runs in. There is no fourth runtime to install, and no new dependency in any manifest.

2. Why each language sits where it does#

Question Answer
why is the capture C++? it is the only process that owns the window handle, the log paths and the device list. A page cannot photograph its own host
why is the window a React page? the app already ships a React 18 + Fluent UI surface (t3-react), with the Documentation page as the working precedent
why is the queue in the platform, in TypeScript? it is a webview panel in a module that already exists; a support inbox is another panel, not another program
why is there no server? every path in the intake document finishes at GitHub's own form or its API, and both accept a request from a browser or a workflow
why is the local Rust service not used for capture? it has no window handle. It stays the origin that serves the page, which is what it already is

3. The message contract#

3.1 The envelope that already exists#

The page and the shell do not trade free text. HandleWebViewMsg (T3000/BacnetWebView.cpp) parses a JSON object, switches on an integer action, and echoes the caller's msgId back:

JSON
{ "action": 41, "msgId": "7" }

The reply carries the action name plus _RES:

JSON
{ "action": "SUPPORT_CAPTURE_RES", "msgId": "7", "ok": true, "path": "D:\\T3000\\Database\\Support\\2026-11-12T09-11-42\\window.png", "width": 1600, "height": 900, "bytes": 421888 }

So the support messages are new enumerators on the existing enum, appended at the end so no existing number moves:

C++
enum WEBVIEW_MESSAGE_TYPE
{
	// ... every existing entry, unchanged ...
	SUPPORT_CONTEXT = 100,
	SUPPORT_CAPTURE,
	SUPPORT_LOGS,
	SUPPORT_SETTINGS,
	SUPPORT_CLIPBOARD,
	SUPPORT_HANDOFF,
	SUPPORT_OPEN_URL,
	SUPPORT_OUTBOX,
	SUPPORT_OUTBOX_RES,
};
Rule Why
append, never renumber the numbers are the wire format, and an old bundle with a new EXE must not call the wrong handler
every reply is { action: "X_RES", msgId, ok } the channel is shared with the rest of the app; a reply without an id cannot be matched to its request
ok: false carries error and never a stack the page shows one sentence and the reason code
the page feature-detects by asking, not by version a bundle can be newer than the EXE; a missing action answers ok: false, error: "unknown_action" and the page hides what needs it

3.2 The eight messages#

Action Request fields Reply
SUPPORT_CONTEXT — version, build, os, locale, screen, panels[] (each name, firmware, product)
SUPPORT_CAPTURE mode: whole | client | screen path, width, height, bytes
SUPPORT_LOGS lines (default 200) path, bytes, dropped (lines removed at the top)
SUPPORT_SETTINGS — path, bytes, or ok: false, error: "withheld"
SUPPORT_CLIPBOARD path ok — whether the PNG reached the clipboard
SUPPORT_HANDOFF bundle (folder), summary ok, route: platform | browser
SUPPORT_OPEN_URL url (https only) ok
SUPPORT_OUTBOX op: save | list | send | delete, bundle items[] for list; ok otherwise

3.3 Threading, and the one trap#

HandleWebViewMsg runs on the UI thread holding handleWebViewMsgMutex. A capture takes tens of milliseconds and the log copy takes more. So:

  • the reply is built after the work, but the work itself is dispatched to a worker thread and the reply posted back with PostWebMessageAsJson when it finishes — the page is already written against a promise with a timeout (§5.3), so a slower reply costs nothing;
  • the capture must run on the thread that owns the window, because PrintWindow needs the window's message loop to be answering — so the pump is kept free by not blocking the lock: capture on the UI thread but outside handleWebViewMsgMutex;
  • the log and settings copies are plain file I/O and run on any thread.

4. The five host methods#

Each one is a small function in one new translation unit. Nothing else in T3000/ changes.

4.1 Capture — SupportCapture.cpp#

The whole method is: get the window's real rectangle, ask it to paint itself into a memory DC with the full-content flag, encode with GDI+, save.

C++
bool CaptureWindow(HWND hwnd, const std::wstring& path, int& width, int& height)
{
	RECT frame = {};
	if (FAILED(DwmGetWindowAttribute(hwnd, DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS, &frame, sizeof(frame)))) {
		GetWindowRect(hwnd, &frame);
	}
	width = frame.right - frame.left;
	height = frame.bottom - frame.top;
	if (width <= 0 || height <= 0) {
		return false;
	}

	HDC screen = GetDC(nullptr);
	HDC memory = CreateCompatibleDC(screen);
	HBITMAP dib = CreateCompatibleBitmap(screen, width, height);
	HGDIOBJ previous = SelectObject(memory, dib);

	const BOOL painted = PrintWindow(hwnd, memory, PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT);

	CLSID png;
	CLSIDFromString(L"{557CF406-1A04-11D3-9A73-0000F81EF32E}", &png);
	Gdiplus::Bitmap bitmap(dib, nullptr);
	const Gdiplus::Status saved = bitmap.Save(path.c_str(), &png, nullptr);

	SelectObject(memory, previous);
	DeleteObject(dib);
	DeleteDC(memory);
	ReleaseDC(nullptr, screen);
	return painted && saved == Gdiplus::Ok;
}
Detail Decision
the flag PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT (0x2) is what makes a WebView2 child appear at all; without it the pane is black
the rectangle DwmGetWindowAttribute(DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS) excludes the invisible resize border and keeps a multi-monitor window on its own monitor; GetWindowRect is the fallback
DPI the app declares no DPI awareness — no manifest entry and no SetProcessDpiAwareness call — so the rectangle it reports is already in the pixels it draws in. The capture therefore never rescales, and the page is told the pixel size it received
the encoder GDI+ is already linked and used (Gdiplus::Font in BacnetGraphic.cpp); PNG needs no new library
the cap if the long edge exceeds 2560 px, scale once with Gdiplus::Bitmap::GetThumbnailImage and re-encode
where it saves <exe>\Database\Support\<timestamp>\window.png, beside the app's own data (g_strExePth), never %TEMP% — plant PCs clean %TEMP% and support loses the file
black output if more than 99 % of pixels are one colour, capture again with client mode and report ok: false, error: "capture_blank" rather than sending a black image

New link dependency: dwmapi.lib for the frame bounds. One line in CMakeLists.txt, next to the WebView2 loader.

4.2 Context — SupportContext.cpp#

Read, do not compute: the version from the app's own version resource, the screen name from the frame's current view, the panels from the already-loaded device list in memory.

Field Source
version, build the executable's VS_VERSIONINFO, as About already reads it
os, locale RtlGetVersion and GetUserDefaultLocaleName — not GetVersionEx, which lies without a manifest
screen the frame's active view title, which the page can cross-check against its own route
panels[] the same list the webview is already given by GET_PANELS_LIST, filtered to those with data on screen

The reply is capped at 4 KB. A panel name is user data, so the field is name and nothing else is read from the device.

4.3 Logs — SupportLog.cpp#

Read the tail, do not load the file: seek to max(0, size - 512 KB), discard the first partial line, keep the last 200 lines, write UTF-8, cap at 256 KB, and record how many lines were discarded in dropped.

Detail Decision
encoding the app's logs are locale-encoded; the excerpt is converted to UTF-8 once, so the page never guesses
redaction the excerpt is not rewritten — the review panel (§8.7 of the intake) shows it whole and lets the person remove the attachment
failure a missing log is ok: true with path: null and bytes: 0, not an error: a report without logs is still a report

4.4 Outbox — SupportOutbox.cpp#

A report is a folder, so it survives a crash between any two writes:

JSON
{
  "id": "2026-11-12T09-11-42",
  "created": "2026-11-12T09:11:42Z",
  "title": "Trendlog graph is empty after I picked 6 points",
  "kind": "bug",
  "state": "queued",
  "files": ["window.png", "t3000-2026-11-12.log"],
  "context": { "version": "2026.0912", "screen": "Devices > Trendlogs" }
}
Operation Method
save write report.json.tmp, flush, rename to report.json — a rename is atomic on NTFS, so a half-written report is never listed
list enumerate <exe>\Database\Support\* for folders with a report.json; ignore the rest
send the same handoff as SUPPORT_HANDOFF, then state: "sent"
delete delete the folder, then report the new list

A state field rather than a move, so a folder never disappears under a running send.

4.5 Handoff — SupportHandoff.cpp#

One function, two routes, and the second is not a fallback in the apologetic sense — it is the normal path on a machine without the platform:

Step What happens
1 ShellExecuteEx with temco-platform://support/new?bundle=<url-encoded folder>
2 ShellExecuteEx returns a value above 32 when the protocol is registered; anything else means no handler
3 on no handler: put the PNG on the clipboard as CF_DIB, then open reportIssueUrl with ?title= and ?body= prefilled
4 reply route: "platform" or route: "browser", so the page can say which one happened
Detail Decision
no shell injection the URL is built from a fixed scheme, a fixed path and one percent-encoded local path. No user text reaches the command line
the clipboard CF_DIB (not CF_HDROP) — a browser accepts a pasted DIB into a file input, and GitHub's attachment box is a file input
the size a prefilled GitHub URL cannot carry a 400 KB image; the URL carries text only, and the image travels by clipboard

4.6 The crash marker#

SetUnhandledExceptionFilter writes one small file before the process dies, and the next start reads it.

JSON
{ "fingerprint": "0xC0000005:trendlog+0x1f42", "first": "2026-11-12T09:11:03Z", "count": 1, "log": "t3000-2026-11-12.log" }
Detail Decision
the fingerprint exception code plus module and offset — stable across runs, distinct across faults, which is what Do not ask again needs
what the handler writes 200 bytes, with CreateFileW(..., FILE_FLAG_WRITE_THROUGH). It does not read the log, build JSON with jsoncpp, or allocate: a handler that allocates can fault again
the full dump left to Windows Error Reporting's LocalDumps key, configured by the installer, not by the app
the counter count is why the third crash of the same fault is reported without asking again

5. The Support page#

5.1 Where it goes#

The app already carries a React surface, so the window is a feature folder, not a new app:

Path What it is
src/t3-react/features/support/pages/SupportPage.tsx the window: header, rail, step content
src/t3-react/features/support/components/ ScreenshotStep, AnnotationCanvas, DetailsStep, ReviewStep, SentStep, OutboxStep, HelpSearch
src/t3-react/features/support/services/supportBridge.ts the promise layer over the message contract (§5.3)
src/t3-react/features/support/support.css or .module.css Fluent tokens only; no hard-coded colour
src/t3-react/app/router/routes.ts one lazy route, in the same table as DocumentationPage

The route is registered exactly like the Documentation page is: lazy() import, inside the existing router table. No new build target, no new entry point — npm run build in the web project picks it up, and npm run deploy:t3000 copies the result into T3000/ResourceFile/webview/www as it does today.

5.2 Components, not inventions#

Need Use
buttons, fields, dropdowns, badges @fluentui/react-components — already a dependency, and it is the same design system the Documentation page uses
light and dark the app's theme folder and its existing Fluent theme provider
icons @fluentui/react-icons, already a dependency
the step rail a <nav> with aria-current="step"; no custom list widget
the annotation surface one <canvas> with pointer events; fabric and paper are already in the app, but plain canvas is enough and is 200 lines
translation the app's existing i18n pipeline (XLIFF, xliff is already a dependency); no second translation system

5.3 The bridge#

One module, one function, and the page never posts a raw message anywhere else:

TypeScript
type Reply = { msgId?: string; ok?: boolean; action?: string; error?: string; [key: string]: unknown };

const pending = new Map<string, (reply: Reply) => void>();
let sequence = 0;

export function request(action: number, fields: Record<string, unknown> = {}, timeoutMs = 8000): Promise<Reply> {
	const msgId = String(++sequence);
	return new Promise<Reply>((resolve, reject) => {
		const timer = setTimeout(() => {
			pending.delete(msgId);
			reject(new Error('bridge_timeout'));
		}, timeoutMs);
		pending.set(msgId, reply => {
			clearTimeout(timer);
			pending.delete(msgId);
			resolve(reply);
		});
		window.chrome.webview.postMessage(JSON.stringify({ action, msgId, ...fields }));
	});
}

window.chrome.webview.addEventListener('message', event => {
	const reply = typeof event.data === 'string' ? JSON.parse(event.data) as Reply : event.data as Reply;
	if (reply.msgId) {
		pending.get(reply.msgId)?.(reply);
	}
});
Rule Why
every call has a timeout a handler that throws must not leave a spinner forever
request is the only writer to chrome.webview the channel is shared with the rest of the app, and a second writer means two listeners and duplicate replies
no reply is trusted for shape the reply is parsed and its fields are checked before use, because it crosses a process boundary
the browser build still loads window.chrome?.webview is undefined in a browser; the module exposes isHosted() and the page runs read-only in a browser for development

5.4 The annotation canvas#

Step Method
load request(SUPPORT_CAPTURE, { mode }) → a path → <img src> served by the local Rust origin, or the host's own file://-equivalent route
draw keep a base image and a list of annotations { tool, from, to, width }; redraw on every pointer move (60 fps on a 1600 × 900 canvas is not a problem)
redact fill the rectangle with black on the export canvas, not only on screen; the exported PNG has no pixels there
export canvas.toBlob('image/png'), then hand the blob back to the host as a path — the host writes it, because the page cannot write to disk
undo pop the annotation list; the base image is never mutated

The one rule that is not negotiable: redaction happens before the file is exported, so no un-redacted copy exists on disk.

5.5 Help & Learn and the offline copy#

The window is loaded from http://localhost:9103, which is served by the Rust service that is already running. So the help copy is:

Piece Method
the copy the site's content package, unpacked beside the app during install — the same tree the site is generated from
search an index built at bundle time (DocFX already emits one); the page filters it in memory, which is why search works with no network
the online half SUPPORT_OPEN_URL opens the real site in the browser
if the service is down the page loads from the bundle's own files (chrome-extension://-style local origin) and hides search; the report half still works

6. The platform surfaces#

Surface Where Method
the protocol handler src/temco/platform/ (one file, one registration) IURLService.registerHandler with an IURLHandler whose handleURL claims support + /new and executes a command
the inbox panel extensions/temco-workbench/src/support.ts vscode.window.createWebviewPanel, in the same shape as dashboard.ts — one panel map, one open()
the issue draft the panel writes draft.md a WorkspaceEdit, so the draft is a real file a person can read, diff and copy
the forum draft the panel, after an approval nothing is posted; the panel shows the text as it would appear
TypeScript
class SupportUrlHandler implements IURLHandler {
	constructor(private readonly commandService: ICommandService) { }

	async handleURL(uri: URI): Promise<boolean> {
		if (uri.authority !== 'support' || uri.path !== '/new') {
			return false;
		}
		const bundle = new URLSearchParams(uri.query).get('bundle') ?? undefined;
		await this.commandService.executeCommand('temcoWorkbench.support.open', bundle);
		return true;
	}
}
Rule Why
the handler returns false for any other URL a protocol handler that swallows every temco-platform:// URL breaks the app's own links
the bundle path is treated as untrusted it arrives from another process. It is resolved, must be inside the app's Database\Support folder, and its files are read with a size cap; nothing is executed and nothing is extracted
the panel loads no remote content a strict CSP, a nonce for the one inline script, and images only through asWebviewUri
one command, one panel reopening the same bundle focuses the existing tab rather than opening a second copy

7. Automation#

Piece Method
the workflow .github/workflows/support-triage.yml, on: issues: [opened, edited], permissions: issues: write
the token secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN only. No PAT, no app key, no repository secret to rotate
classify a table in the workflow: label keywords → area:trendlogs, area:bacnet, area:graphics; the issue template's own labels do the type
dedupe gh issue list --search "<two distinctive words>" --state all, then link the closest rather than guess
the comment one comment, posted once, with an <!-- support-triage --> marker so a re-run edits instead of stacking
the draft a Copilot/LLM step only when a repository variable enables it; the fallback is the same comment without prose
docs-owed when the body names a help page id, add docs-owed; that label already exists for the site's own checks
the forum never automated. The draft is approved by a person (§9.3 of the intake)

8. Nothing new is installed#

Layer New dependency
C++ dwmapi.lib — a Windows SDK import library, not a package
web UI none: React, Fluent UI, Router, Vitest and canvas are all present
Rust none: the service is unchanged, and no support route is added to it in phase 1 or 2
platform none: IURLService, webview panels and the command registry are the fork's own
automation none: gh is preinstalled on GitHub's runners

If a later phase wants one-click anonymous filing (§13 of the intake), the smallest addition is a single Cloudflare Worker or Azure Function — not a service in this repository, and not a token in the client.

9. Failure modes and what the user sees#

Failure Detection What the page does
the web bundle is newer than the EXE SUPPORT_CONTEXT answers unknown_action hides the capture step, keeps the form, hands off through the browser route
the capture is black the host's pixel check says so, offers client mode, and offers the whole-screen capture
the log is missing path: null the attachment is absent from the review, with one line saying why
no platform installed ShellExecuteEx ≤ 32 the browser route, with the clipboard message
no connection the page's own navigator.onLine and the first failed handoff saves to the outbox and says when it will leave
the outbox is full more than 20 queued reports refuses a new save and offers to send or delete
the local service is down the page's fetch fails renders from bundled files, search hidden, report intact
the platform is given a bad bundle the path escapes the support folder, or a file is over the cap the panel shows the problem and offers the log, and posts nothing

Every one of these is a sentence in the window, not a dialog with an error code.

10. Budget#

Thing Target Why
the page's own assets ≤ 40 KB gzipped it joins a 33 MB bundle; this is noise, and a feature folder that pulls in a chart library would not be
cold open ≤ 200 ms on a 1366 × 768 plant PC it opens from localhost, with no network
the capture ≤ 120 ms for a 1600 × 900 window it runs on the UI thread
the PNG ≤ 1.5 MB, long edge ≤ 2560 px it is pasted into a browser or attached to an issue
the bundle ≤ 2 MB zipped the outbox is a folder on a plant PC's disk
the platform panel ≤ 150 ms to first paint it reads one folder of local files

11. How each part ships#

Artifact Built by Reaches the customer by
T3000.exe with the support module CMake, the existing target — one added source file and dwmapi.lib the existing installer
the web bundle with the Support page npm run build in the web project, then npm run deploy:t3000 the same bundle path the Documentation page already uses, and T3000's own updater
the offline help copy the site's content package the installer
the platform panel the extension build the platform's normal release
the workflow committed YAML takes effect on merge

The only version handshake is the one the page performs itself: it asks the host what it can do and adapts. There is no separate protocol version to keep in step.

12. Work breakdown#

In the order that keeps every step shippable.

# Task Where Done when
1 SUPPORT_CONTEXT and SUPPORT_HANDOFF, browser route only T3000/Support*.cpp, BacnetWebView.cpp Help ▸ Report an Issue opens GitHub with the title prefilled
2 SUPPORT_CAPTURE and SUPPORT_CLIPBOARD T3000/SupportCapture.cpp, dwmapi.lib the screenshot pastes into the issue body from the clipboard
3 the Support page, steps 1–4, no annotation src/t3-react/features/support/ a report is written in the window and handed off
4 the annotation canvas and redaction the same folder a redacted area is gone from the exported PNG
5 SUPPORT_LOGS, SUPPORT_SETTINGS and the review panel C++ and the page an attachment can be read and removed before sending
6 the outbox SupportOutbox.cpp a report written offline leaves on the next start
7 the crash marker and the next-start prompt SupportCrash.cpp a killed process produces one prompt, fingerprinted
8 Help & Learn over the offline copy the page, and the installer's copy search answers with the network off
9 the protocol handler and the inbox panel src/temco, extensions/temco-workbench a bundle opens as a tab, and the reply is copied by hand
10 the triage workflow .github/workflows/support-triage.yml a new issue is labelled and answered once

13. Validation#

Layer What proves it
C++ a support-selftest switch that captures the main window and writes a PNG, run by hand on a Windows build; the log reader and the outbox have plain unit tests
the page Vitest, already configured: the bridge's promise, timeout and unknown-action behaviour; the redaction export
the platform the existing test harness with a fake IURLService, and a bundle-path rejection test
the docs npm run check-temco-docs, which already runs in npm run check-temco
the end to end a scripted Windows run: open T3000, trigger a report, confirm the issue opens with title and body, and the clipboard holds the PNG
