ui/editor-design.title: The editor
ui/editor-design.html:
The design for R6 — editing and publishing: the toolbar, creating a document, images, drafts, and where the review happens. It is written the same week its first step was built, so it separates what exists from what is proposed, and it puts the one decision that is not mine in front of the person who has to make it.

The content rules are not here. Registry schema, link forms, media rules, review flow and publishing belong to design/temco-learn/, which stays the source of truth; this document only says how the desktop application implements them.

1. The surface: VS Code's editor, with the project's toolbar on it#

15-online-editor.md designs the hosted editor: Monaco, bundled and self-hosted, with an API behind it, served by the center tool on a host that has a clone. That editor is not this application's editor and building it twice would be the bug.

the hosted editor this application
the core Monaco, bundled by us, ~2 MB, custom build, <textarea> fallback VS Code is Monaco plus a shell — nothing to bundle
what it adds toolbar, preview pane, gate markers, upload, publish, PR toolbar, a link to a real page, the outline, the gates' markers — of which the markers already exist (src/diagnostics.ts)
what it never does never WYSIWYG: a rich round-trip rewrites the line layout of the whole file the same rule, and the same reason
publishing POST /api/docs/publish → a real PR never. This application builds and reports; shipping stays a separate act

So the desktop equivalent of "Monaco + the toolbar + completion + markers" is VS Code, with the toolbar built — which is what src/format.ts now is. An editor page of the project's own, hosting Monaco in a webview, was considered and is refused for the reason 15-online-editor.md, What is not built gives for the website: the integration is the part that matters, and the editor is the part that already exists.

What exists — the toolbar, built#

Sixteen commands, all temcoDocs.format.*, in src/format.ts. Each one edits the buffer in front: the page a person is typing in, undone with Ctrl+Z. None of them writes a file, opens a tab, or touches the registry.

Where a person meets it What is there
the editor's title bar, Markdown files only Bold · Italic · Link to a page · Format
the editor's context menu, and the tab's the submenu Temco Docs — all sixteen, grouped
the palette every action, by name; Format lists them all in one picker
Group Actions
Inline Bold **…** · Italic *…* · Inline code `…`
Blocks Heading level (##–####) · bullet · numbered · task · block quote · code block with a language · table · horizontal rule · callout
Insert Link · Link to a page
Navigate Go to a heading (this page's outline)

Three things it does on purpose, each of which has an obvious wrong answer:

  • Every button is a toggle. Bold over **bold** removes the marks; the bullet list over a list takes the bullets off; the same heading level again removes it. That is what a button does in every other editor.
  • A block gets a blank line before it when the line above is prose. Not decoration: text followed by --- is a level-2 heading in Markdown, and a table glued to a paragraph is a paragraph.
  • A callout, a fence and an alert marker start their own line — mid-line they would glue to the text after the cursor, and > [!NOTE] is an alert only at the start of a line.

No keybindings are contributed, deliberately. Ctrl+B hides the side bar everywhere else, and this extension has to keep working in an ordinary VS Code. Everything here is a command, so a chord is one personal binding away.

A page that is not a file on disk says so. A page read from a source, or a diff, has a scheme that is not file, and every action refuses it in words rather than appearing to work.

2. Creating a document#

A page is a file, not a pair — and that is the product repository's own doing. This section said the opposite when it was first written, so the correction is worth stating plainly, with where it comes from. T3000Webview-EEZ-Studio/scripts/docs-registry.mjs generates the entries:

Text
  buildPages(existing)                    walks docs/t3000/** and docs/legacy/**
    id      = the docs-relative path without `.md`      the page id *is* the path
    title   = prev.title  ??  the file's first `#`      ← so a skeleton starts with one
    area    = the top folder      chapter = the second path segment (or `(root)`)
    order   = prev.order  ??  10, 20, 30… inside the chapter
    owner   = 'docs'   ship = true for t3000   tags/keywords/code = []
    every field:  prev.<field> ?? a default             ← an existing (curated) value always wins
  and the file itself is written with  JSON.stringify(registry, null, 2) + '\n'

So creating a page writes no entry at all: the file goes in, the repository's own generator — which this application already runs as one of its allowlisted scripts — adds the entry, derives its place, and takes its title from the first heading. What only a person curates is order, chapter, title, owner, tags and code, and those are the values the generator then leaves alone. Section 5 is that decision, as taken.

Two consequences for the flow below, both now built: a new page is a file and a generator run, offered in that order; and there is no "loose page" kind, because the exclude key the design package's schema describes is not produced by this repository's generator — a Markdown file under docs/ that no area covers is an unregistered page error, not a working note.

The kinds worth offering#

Kind The headings it starts with Why it is a kind
Article Overview · Configuration · Related pages the ordinary case
Task Before you start · Steps · If it does not work the commonest documentation shape
Reference Fields · Notes the shape an API or a register actually has
Troubleshooting Symptom · Cause · Fix matches the troubleshooting area the product already has
Release note What is new · Fixed · Known issues what changed in a build

Each skeleton is headings only — no invented sentences, because a template that writes prose is a template someone has to delete. Every one starts with # <title>, which is what the generator reads.

The flow, as built#

Text
  New page ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  1  Where    the row it was started from — a page's own area and chapter, a chapter itself,
              an area's root chapter — or the row you have selected, or:
              which source ▸ which area ▸ which chapter
  2  Kind     article · task · reference · troubleshooting · release note
  3  Title    Trend Logs
  4  File     trend-logs          →  docs/t3000/features/trend-logs.md        (shown, not guessed)
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  [ Write the page ]  ── it starts as “# Trend Logs” and the kind's headings
  ── then ──
  “It becomes a page when the registry names it.”          [ Run the generator ]

A repository row cannot answer step 1 — it is not in an area — so it answers the source and the rest is still asked. Nothing else is asked when the kind came from the New Page of a Kind submenu: step 2 is the entry that was clicked, and steps 3 and 4 follow as they always do.

New chapter is the same flow with the folder named first, because a chapter is a page's path: a folder with nothing in it is not a chapter, not in the registry, and not in the table of contents. The folder arrives with its first page.

3. Images#

An image is the one action in the toolbar that is missing, and the reason is not the code: the file has to be written into the page's own media/ folder before ![alt](media/…) points at anything.

The rules are already written down, in the design package, so they are not ours to invent:

Rule Source
the file goes into the page's own media/, with a slugified name (02-run-screen.png) 15-online-editor.md, Uploads
accepted: PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF, SVG — diagrams as SVG, sanitised on the way in 15-online-editor.md, Uploads
images ≤ 2 MB · a page ≤ 1 MB · content-type sniffed, never trusted from the name 15-online-editor.md, Safety rules, rule 2
the destination is derived, never supplied 15-online-editor.md, Safety rules, rule 1
screenshots are captured properly or not at all — no editing, no resizing 15-online-editor.md, What is not built

What an extension can and cannot take. A file the user picked (showOpenDialog), a file dropped on the page and an image already on the clipboard are all reachable — the last one not through the extension API, which exposes the clipboard's text only. On Windows the module reads the bitmap itself (System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard, one child process per capture), which is what makes Ctrl+Alt+V work; the loop it belongs to, and what is still missing from it, is authoring-flow.md.

4. Drafts, review and publishing#

Not built, and the largest piece of R6. The design is already fixed and is not ours to change:

where it belongs
editing a local source in place — the page file is the page, which the Workspace view already does
editing a git source on a draft branch in a materialised clone — which is the fetch read mode R2 still owes
review docs:blocking, registry --check, the link check and the media check, run by the repository's own scripts
publishing never from this application: the gates, the commit and the PR are the product repository's
a page's fields in the editor restricted by 15-online-editor.md, Safety rules, rule 4: structure needs the docs owner

So the honest order is: images and create-a-page first, because both need only a decision; drafts after, because they need the fetch mode and a review flow that lives in the product repository.

5. The decision, as taken#

The question was how far this application may go into a product repository. The answer, in the three parts it was asked in:

Asked Taken So the code does this
The Library's title bar holds twelve buttons three inline, the rest in the view's ⋯ newProject · openProjects · openNeeds stay in group navigation; everything else moved to named groups, which is how a view/title item lands in the overflow menu. The header starts work; a row and a page operate on a thing — and the target-less ones ask which, which they already did
Which operations the Workspace tree grows all five: new page · new chapter · rename the title · move (up, down, and by dragging) · retire src/pageOps.ts — six commands, a TreeDragAndDropController, and one modal per write
How far into registry.json one named value, on a confirmation src/registryEdit.ts — title, order, chapter, deprecated, superseded_by, and nothing else; never a whole-file rewrite

Where a row offers its operations was settled on the third attempt: the row menu is the Explorer's, the toolbar mirrors it, and the hover carries nothing. A left click does what it does in the Explorer — opens a page, expands a folder — and a right click (or the keyboard's menu key) opens New Page… · New Chapter… · New Page of a Kind ▸ · Reveal in Explorer · Open in Integrated Terminal · Copy Path · Copy Relative Path · Rename the Title… · Move the Page Up · Move the Page Down · Retire… · Open the Registry, each item only where it means something. The view's … shows the same list — plus New page, New chapter, Refresh, Home and Validate — acting on the row the tree last had focused, which is also what makes it usable from the palette: a view title action is run with the tree pane's context, and every row command falls back to the view's own selection. There are no hover icons on a row: a menu started from a row can only ever be a quick pick in the middle of the top of the window, and that is exactly what the row menu above replaces.

What each operation writes#

Text
 operation                        what changes on disk                          state
 ──────────────────────────────── ───────────────────────────────────────────── ──────────────
 Open · Reveal · the outline       nothing                                      built
 Create the missing page file      one empty .md (declared, absent)             built (earlier)
 New page in this chapter          one .md from a kind's skeleton               built
   → then the repo's docs:registry (its own script; adds the entry)             offered, not forced
 New chapter                       …the same, with the folder named first       built
 Rename the title                  title in registry.json (+ the page's first #) built
 Move up / Move down / drag        order in registry.json — two numbers, swapped built
 Drop on another chapter           chapter + order — *structure*, docs owner     built
 Retire a page                     deprecated + superseded_by                    built
 Rename or move the FILE           the page id — inbound links break            **never**, by rule
 An image into the page's media/   a new file, binary                            **not built** — see the API in `15-online-editor.md`

Four rules hold the writes together, and each one is a decision rather than an implementation detail:

  • A move is a swap, never a renumbering. Placing a page between two others by rewriting every order in the chapter is the generator's own job — it hands out 10, 20, 30… to whatever nobody curated. So a move writes two numbers and the diff is two lines.
  • The file is never renamed or moved. The page id is the path (05-content-and-registry.md, Page ids and aliases), so a page is renamed by changing what it is called: one string in the registry, plus the page's own # heading when it says the same words — two answers to one question otherwise.
  • A chapter change says the word structure. 15-online-editor.md, Safety rules, rule 4 marks chapter as the docs owner's to change, so the confirmation says so and asks for a line in the pull request.
  • Retirement is not deletion. The file stays; the registry records the replacement; the redirect for a retired page is generated by the repository's own pipeline (14-governance.md, Deprecation and retirement).

The evidence for "one value, and nothing else"#

src/registryEdit.ts renders the file the way the repository's own generator writes it — JSON.stringify with two spaces, one trailing newline — and with the file's own line endings, because a clone checked out on Windows is CRLF while the generator emits LF, and a write that flipped every ending would be a diff of the whole file. With both right, the guarantee is testable, so it was tested:

Check Result
the real docs/help/registry.json — 318 pages, 124 KB — opened, re-rendered, compared byte-for-byte identical
a drag into another chapter, diffed line by line against the original two lines changed: chapter and order
a drag onto a sibling, same chapter two lines changed, the two order values swapped
a drop on the page's own chapter nothing written, and it says so
a rename, diffed one line changed, plus the page's own heading
a new page the file written, the registry untouched, then the generator offered

Running the generator afterwards is what keeps the file canonical: the values written here are the ones the generator's own prev.<field> ?? default rule preserves, so nothing is lost by it and nothing here duplicates it.

6. Acceptance, per step#

# Step The test that ends it
1 the toolbar done — a Markdown file shows the four buttons; every button toggles; --- after prose is not a heading; the page picker inserts a link the gate resolves; a page read from a source is refused in words
2 operating on a page done — a page is created from its kind's skeleton and the generator is offered next; a title is renamed and the registry diff is one line; a page is dragged into another chapter and the diff is the two values; retiring one writes deprecated and the replacement and keeps the file
3 insert an image a dropped PNG lands in the page's media/ under a slugified name and is referenced relatively; a 3 MB PNG and a .exe renamed .png are both refused, in words, with the limit
4 drafts a page is corrected, the gates run, the diff is reviewed, and the result is a commit a person made — not one this application made

The evidence for "one value, and nothing else"

ui/platform-design.title: The platform
ui/platform-design.html:
The center documentation platform. One internal application — VS Code plus this extension — that takes documentation from many kinds of source, lets people manage and edit it, and builds the final documents: a site, a CHM, a PDF. A local AI reads the history of those sources and drafts the updates. Everything it knows lives in a local SQLite catalog.

This document is the platform's own design. The content rules — the registry schema, the checks, the review flow, the publishing engine — are the design package in design/temco-learn/, which stays the source of truth.

How Microsoft's own documentation is managed, for comparison#

Worth stating, because it is the shape being copied:

  • A docset is a set of Markdown pages plus a table of contents, living in a repository (Microsoft's own docs are a private repo of Markdown).
  • Metadata on each page — author, ms.topic, ms.date — decides where it appears and who owns it.
  • Monikers are version markers: one page can serve several product versions, and the build emits the right one per version.
  • A build pipeline turns the docset into the published site, and separately into an offline PDF.
  • The reader gets one searchable site; the authoring side (review, status, ownership) is internal.

The equivalents: docset ≈ a Document, moniker ≈ its version, pipeline ≈ its recipe. The difference is where it runs: theirs is a hosted service, ours is an internal app on the maintainer's machine — and ours must also produce the CHM, which theirs does not.

The model: sources → documents → artifacts#

The unit of work is not a repository. A repository is where content may start; the thing a person creates, owns, versions and builds is a document — "T3000 Developer Help", shipped as t3000_dev.chm; "T3000Webview Guide", shipped as t3000_webview.pdf.

Text
  SOURCES  (many kinds — where content comes from)          DOCUMENTS  (what a person creates and manages)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐              ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ git     T3000Webview @ main              │              │ T3000 Developer Help          v1.4     │
  │ git     T3_Engine     @ release/2.1      │ ─── cites ──►│   sources: the first two               │
  │ folder  C:\docs\t3000-extra              │              │   recipe:  chm + pdf + site            │
  │ folder  C:\docs\legacy (markdown tree)   │              │   pages:   318   owner: docs           │
  │ archive a supplier's PDF, read-only      │              │   version: 1.4   audience: developers  │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘              └──────────────┬─────────────────────────┘
                    │                                                      │ build
                    │ materialise / read                                   ▼
                    │                                    ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
                    └──────► AI over history ────────────►│ ARTIFACTS  t3000_dev.chm  1.2 MB  ✔    │
                             summary · pages · drafts    │            t3000_dev.pdf  4.8 MB  ✔    │
                                                         │            the package  published ✔    │
                                                         └────────────────────────────────────────┘

Source — where content comes from. Not necessarily GitHub, not necessarily a repository, not necessarily Markdown:

Kind Examples What the platform does
git any remote: GitHub, GitLab, a bare path — owner/repo@branch reads the tree, the history and the diffs
folder a docfx project, a Markdown tree, loose HTML, images reads it in place; never moves it
archive a supplier's PDF, a vendor's ZIP of pages inventories it, read-only, for reference and search

The branch is chosen per source, defaulting to the repository's own default (main), and reported when the documentation is not on it.

Document — what a person creates: a name, its sources and their branches, a recipe (how to build it), a version, an audience, an owner, and the outputs it must produce. This is the platform's unit of management, and it is what the generator, the builds, the health and the AI are all about.

Artifact — a file a build produced: path, size, time, hash, and which document and source revision it came from.

Build — one run of a document's recipe at a source revision: a job with a log, a status, and the artifacts it left behind. Success is an artifact that did not exist before, never an exit code.

Analysis — what the local AI did over the history: a summary of a commit, the pages it affects, a draft, and what is still owed.

The catalog#

The platform's memory: documents, sources, builds, artifacts, commits and what changed since you last looked. Relational, long-lived, queryable offline.

Where: context.globalStorageUri of the store module — a catalog.db and a sources/ cache of materialised trees. One window, one file, opened by the module that owns it: a caller that opened it with its own storage would find an empty database beside its own code. Never inside a repository, never committed, never in a product's git history.

SQL
sources     id · kind(git|folder|archive) · name · remote_url · path · default_branch · branch
            last_fetch_at · last_commit_sha · last_commit_at · size_bytes · state

documents   id · name · slug · version · audience · owner · recipe(kind) · created_at · updated_at

doc_sources document_id · source_id · include_glob · branch · role(primary|supplement)

recipes     document_id · engine(docfx|own-script|chm|pdf|site) · config_path · script · outputs_json

builds      id · document_id · started_at · finished_at · status · revision · log_path

artifacts   id · build_id · document_id · path · bytes · built_at · sha256 · kind(chm|pdf|site|zip)

commits     sha · source_id · at · author · subject · summary · summary_model · summarised_at

commit_pages  commit_sha · page_id · how(code-glob|path|terms)

pages       id · document_id · source_id · path · title · owner · reviewed_at · stale · counts_json

scans       id · source_id · at · mode(local|fetch|api) · revision · counts_json

events      id · at · kind · subject_kind · subject_id · detail · seen_at
            kind ∈ { new_source, docs_found, registry_found, push, pages_changed,
                     docs_removed, branch_mismatch, build_ok, build_failed, draft_ready }

Every view is a query over these rows. Nothing is asked of the network twice, and the last scan is readable with the network unplugged — and says when it was taken.

Reading a source: three ways, and when to use which#

The user's requirement — "load the source code… download to a local temp folder or read it from online" — is two mechanisms with different costs, and the platform picks per job:

Mode How Used for Cost
local a folder you have open, or a path in the catalog everything: files, checks, edits, builds none
materialised a shallow fetch into globalStorage/sources/<slug> — git clone --filter=blob:none --depth 1, or a fetch of the needed range — on a scratch branch the platform owns drafts (the model needs the page text), builds, file-existence checks disk, bounded
online the host's API for one commit's changed files and patches commit summaries, "what changed" — diffs only, no clone API calls, bounded

The rule that picks between the last two: summaries need diffs; drafts need files. A commit summary over an API patch is cheap and needs no clone; a draft needs the real page, so the platform materialises the source once and reuses it. A patch can be truncated for a very large file — the summary records that it was, rather than guessing.

Caps, because this is a maintainer's PC: a source cache budget (default 2 GB) with LRU eviction, a maximum fetch depth, a maximum commits analysed per run, and a Prune the source cache command. Nothing is ever fetched without a command or a queue the user started.

The AI over history, per source#

Text
   commits since the last scan   ──►  summarise what it did, in the product's words
       (API patches, or the local clone)      │
                                              ├──► which pages it affects
                                              │      code globs from the registry, else path, else terms
                                              ├──► draft the page edits  (local model, draft-only)
                                              └──► add to the owed list
   ▲  nothing here publishes, commits or approves: a named person does that

Summaries, their model and their time are stored, so a summary is computed once and is visible offline. The whole pass is a job with progress — resumable, bounded per run, and honest about what it skipped.

Creating a document#

Create a document asks for the few facts the catalog needs, and nothing more:

A document can be created before its sources are perfect — that is the point. The platform records what it found, says what is missing, and offers the next step.

Editing and writing#

  • A local source is edited in place — the page file is the page, as the Content view already does.
  • A git source is edited on a draft branch in the materialised clone: the AI's diff is applied there, the user reviews it, and they commit or open a PR. The platform never commits on anyone's behalf.
  • Nothing under _admin/ or _edit/ is ever written — 00-architecture.md calls those generated pages, not documentation.
  • The hosted editor stays the design package's web surface; this is its desktop equivalent.

Telling the user — quietly#

Unseen events become one grouped notification, never one per event, and seen_at is stamped when the group is shown or dismissed so a fact is never announced twice. Default docs-only: a daily summary of documentation change, no modals. A Since you last looked node heads the view.

Feasibility#

Yes. It is a catalog, a few connectors, a build runner and the AI that already exists — no new engine, and no server. The real constraints, each with its answer:

Constraint Answer
The database — decided node:sqlite: it ships with the extension host's Node, so there is no dependency to add a build whose Node predates 22.5 is refused in words by the store, at the point of use. The engines.vscode floor should be raised once the first F5 confirms the built-in is present
Disk — cached source trees grow a budget (2 GB default), LRU eviction, Prune the source cache, and a .gitignore-aware size report
The network — a whole-organisation read and commit patches need rate limit a token in secret storage (5,000 calls/hour), and online mode on demand only. The 60-call limit has been reached in practice; it is not an optional convenience
Time — AI summaries over history are slow a job queue with progress, a per-run cap, resumable, and summaries stored once
Many kinds of local documentation one ingester per kind, starting with: a Markdown tree, a docfx project, and an inventory-only reader for HTML and PDF
Trust — this is the maintainer's machine all state in globalStorageUri; nothing written into a repository; nothing fetched without a command or a queue the user started

Surfaces#

The platform has two lists in the sidebar and rich pages in the editor area. Nothing else competes for attention: a document is managed from its page, a source is read from its row, and the AI is beside whatever you are working on.

What opens when the platform is activated is the project you are on — its dashboard, the one surface that says what is in it and what next — then the page you were last working on, then the home page when there is neither. temcoWorkbench.start.open (project · page · home · welcome · none) chooses, and none opens no tab at all for anyone who would rather nothing opened by itself. The side panel the window is revealed on is a second, separate choice — temcoWorkbench.start.panel, whose values are the left panel's own items (Home, Documentation, Repositories, AI, Forum, Tools, Settings) and whose default is temcoDashboard.

The Workspace is the first view, and the Library is beneath it. Both sit in the temco activity bar: the Workspace tree is the documentation module's, the Library is the workbench's — the one index of everything every module has. The Workspace shows the project being worked on and never the open folders, so the registry checks, the status bar and the faults follow the project too — a tree built from whatever happens to be open would be a second, unrelated answer to the same question. The view is never hidden and never blank: with nothing to show it carries rows that say why and offer the one act that fills it (no project yet → create one; no project is being worked on → choose one in the Library; this project has nothing to show → open it and read its sources). Those rows are drawn by the tree itself — viewsWelcome was tried first and dropped, because a welcome's when clause is resolved when the view is first painted, which is before the refresh has read anything: it announced "nothing recorded yet" over a catalog that held five projects.

With exactly one project recorded there is nothing to choose between, so it selects itself and the tree is ready without anyone picking it; that is not a person choosing, so the sidebar is left where it was. Choosing a project afterwards brings the Workspace forward, and clearing one brings the Library back — the two views are a sequence, and only a click walks it.

The Library's Projects row (extensions/temco-workbench/src/views.ts) is the list of what this application manages. Each project's row carries what a project is made of and what can be done with it — the four technical facts are on the row and its children, so nothing has to be opened to decide: version · owner · outputs; its sources with how many pages each holds and how it was read; how many pages, how many without an owner, how many artifacts and when the last one was built; and the operations — Work on it · Open · Read sources · Build · Edit · Remove…. The one being worked on is first and marked, because the panel is read top-down.

A page for a project that has been removed closes itself, and the projects page takes its place. The first version kept the tab and put a notice in it — which was wrong twice over. It cleared document.body, taking the tabs, the actions and every element the next render writes into with it, so the tab could never become another project's page; and it left a page about nothing, with working-looking buttons on it. A tab for something that no longer exists is worse than no tab: the removal says so in one message, closes that page, and opens the list of what is left. Removal from any surface does this, and a page opened for a project that is not there does the same thing rather than rendering.

There is no Work view. It was a second copy of the tree's Gaps list plus a counter, in a third place, behind one icon that meant five things at once — decided with the user. What replaced it:

  • the sidebar's Library holds one expandable Needs attention row: a count line, the missing-file row, a stale row, an unowned row, then the faulty pages, then More…
  • More… (or the row's title, or the row's title-bar button) opens What needs doing — a page with the room to say why each thing is listed and where the fix is: sources · faults · declared-but-missing · stale · no owner · owed. A missing file is created from there with one click, which is the one write this application is allowed
  • each mark means one thing: ⊗ a structural fault, ! a declared page whose file is absent, ↺ the generator's stale verdict, ▲ an unowned page, ⇄ owed
  • the staleness report moved to the Library's title bar, where the view it belonged to used to be

Owed is never computed here. Documentation owed is the product repository's own gate — scripts/docs-owed.mjs, npm run docs:owed, waivers that expire (11-review-and-cicd.md) — so the page runs that script as a task and reports what a run is: where, when, the exit code. Its output, in the terminal, is the verdict, and the page says so. A second opinion about what is owed is the one thing a documentation platform must not invent.

The selection is state, in one place (extensions/temco-store/src/selection.ts, in workspaceState): which project, and which page of it you were last on. A project belongs to the window, not the machine — two windows on two products must not answer about each other's pages. Opening a project makes it the one being worked on, and the library row, the view's description and the dashboard all say so; a project that is removed while selected clears the selection rather than leaving a view about something that is not there.

On activation, nothing has to be clicked. The one project with nothing chosen selects itself (with two or more nothing is guessed — see Surfaces); the Workspace view arrives with the only repository's areas open and their chapters beneath them; the Library opens Projects, so the names of what you have are on screen; and the tab that opens is the welcome page (temcoWorkbench.start.open, default welcome), or — once that checkbox is off — the selected project's pages, then the page you were last on, then the overview. A tree that re-decided itself after every refresh would be worse than one that never opened at all, so a person's own expand or collapse is remembered for the session and beats both defaults — a refresh re-reads the data, never the layout (extensions/temco-workbench/src/views.ts).

The window#

As built$2 The figures below are the design; what exists is these same surfaces with different names, and the difference is recorded here rather than left to be discovered:

  • The sidebar holds three sections in one container, not two: Workspace (the page tree, the first thing built), Work (what needs doing — faults per open folder, and changes not yet shown), Library (the projects, the sources with their pages beneath them, and the catalog's own state).
  • The unit is called a project in everything a person reads. The catalog's table is still documents; a project is what that row is, and renaming the table buys nothing but a migration.
  • Four pages, one job each. The hub (extensions/temco-projects/src/projectHub.ts) is what one project is — Overview · Pages · Sources · AI · Builds, with Read and Build at the top; the list of projects is the Library's Projects row, not a page of its own. The edit page (extensions/temco-projects/src/projectPage.ts) is what it is made of. Opening the editor for every look at a project would make reading its pages and editing its fields the same act, so they are separate commands (openProject and editProject). The dashboard (extensions/temco-workbench/src/home.ts) is the application itself, and the AI page (extensions/temco-ai/src/aiPage.ts) is the AI. All four are tabs in one group.
  • The project's pages are tabs in one group, and so are the documentation pages they open — never a split. The rule lives in extensions/temco-ui/src/columns.ts and is stated there once, together with the two wrong answers that led to it: a page opened Beside produced a second column a few hundred pixels wide, and "is the tab in front one of ours?" — tried twice — is not a question a webview tab answers reliably. So the file asks nothing about what is in front; it finds the group that already holds a page of ours and opens there, which makes one group the only outcome. reveal with that column also moves a page a previous layout left in a second group, so the split heals the next time the page is opened. ViewColumn is named in exactly one place in the whole source.
  • The layout survives a narrow column. Every grid is minmax(min(Nem, 100%), 1fr), every flex child that holds text is min-width: 0, and a table wider than the pane scrolls inside its own box. A bare minmax(Nem, 1fr) sets a hard floor that pushed the right-hand column out of the pane — the page scrolled sideways instead of reflowing, and it looked like a rendering fault rather than a CSS one.
  • The AI page (extensions/temco-ai/src/aiPage.ts) is the AI as something owned and configured — the four facts a person needs before trusting an answer, what can be downloaded, and which is chosen. It stands beside the AI panel: the panel is the conversation, the page is the setup. A project's AI tab carries the same facts plus the suggestions read from that project's pages.
  • Suggestions need no model. The ones on the AI tab — an unowned page, a source never read, a chapter past about 25 pages, a repeated title — come from the catalog, so they are identical with the AI off. What a model adds is prose over the same facts, never the facts themselves.

The AI goes on the right, beside the page being worked on — that is where app-layout.md's mock puts it, and it is where a reader of a page wants a question answered.

The AI sits in the right side bar, and that is a declaration, not a preference. The container is contributed under contributes.viewsContainers.secondarySidebar — a location VS Code's own schema has, and which this design document wrongly claimed did not exist. The secondary side bar is therefore its default home: nothing to drag, nothing to pick, no setup step. If someone moves it (the panel, the primary side bar), Show the AI in the right side bar (temcoAi.dockRight, in the temco-ai module) focuses the view and invokes the per-container <containerId>.resetViewContainerLocation command VS Code registers, which returns it to its declared location. That is also why the extension never asks where a view currently is: the view-location API is not exposed to extensions, and the reset command makes the question unnecessary.

An image is the one button that is not here, and the reason is the write rule rather than the code: the file has to be written into the page's own media/ before the reference to it points at anything.   ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Since you last looked
    ● T3000 Developer Help      12 pages changed · built 2 days ago · 2 drafts waiting
    ● C:\docs\t3000-extra       new folder found · 34 pages · never built

  DOCUMENT                VERSION  SOURCES  PAGES  HEALTH  LAST PUSH          STATE
  T3000 Developer Help    1.4      2        318    82      main 2 days ago    ok · 12 stale · 3 unowned
    ├ 12 stale pages — the code they claim moved on since the last review

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  4 documents · 6 sources · 468 pages · 1 source has no registry yet

  (nothing here yet)   No documents yet.  [ Create a document ]   [ Scan for sources ]

Sources — what the platform reads from#

Text
  KIND     SOURCE                      BRANCH      REGISTRY  DOCS   PAGES  LAST PUSH          READ AS
  git      T3000Webview                main        —         yes    318    main 2 days ago    fetch
    └ registry is on feature/lvgl-svg-renderer, not on main          ⚠ branch mismatch
  git      T3_Engine                   release/2.1 yes       yes     96    rel/2.1 5 months    api · floor
  git      T3000-API                   main        —         —        —     main 3 years       api · floor
  folder   C:\docs\t3000-extra         —           —         yes     34    —                  local
  folder   C:\docs\legacy              —           yes       yes    104    —                  local
  archive  vendor\bacnet-stack.pdf     —           —         —        —     —                  read-only
  … 17 more repositories with no documentation found

  [ Scan for sources ]  [ Add a source… ]  [ Prune the source cache (1.8 GB of 2 GB) ]

Create a document#

Text
  ┌─ Create a document ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  1  Name        T3000 Developer Help    version 1.4    audience developers    owner docs   │
  │                                                                                           │
  │  2  Sources — pick from what the catalog knows                         [ + Add a source ]  │
  │     [x] T3000Webview    branch [ main ▾ ]    318 pages · registry —        ⚠ see below      │
  │     [x] C:\docs\t3000-extra                  34 pages · no registry                       │
  │     [ ] T3_Engine       branch [ rel/2.1 ▾ ]  96 pages · registry yes                      │
  │       the platform says what it found:                                                    │
  │         the registry is on feature/lvgl-svg-renderer, not main   → [ use that branch ]     │
  │         C:\docs\t3000-extra has 34 pages and no registry         → [ start one ]          │
  │                                                                                           │
  │  3  Recipe      engine [ docfx ▾ ]   config docs/docfx.json                                │
  │     outputs     [x] CHM t3000_dev.chm  [x] PDF t3000_dev.pdf  [ ] publish to the site     │
  │     it runs the repository's own script, as a task — never a re-implementation             │
  │                                                                                           │
  │  4  Review      T3000 Developer Help v1.4 · 2 sources · 352 pages · chm + pdf              │
  │                 first build:  npm run docs:registry  then  npm run docs:site               │
  │                                                     [ Back ]  [ Create ]  [ Create & build]│
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Reading a source — three modes#

Text
  local      a folder you have open, or a path in the catalog
             files · checks · edits · builds                                    cost: none

  fetch      a shallow clone into  globalStorage/sources/<slug>
             git clone --filter=blob:none --depth 1                             cost: disk (2 GB, LRU)
             used for: drafts (the model needs the page text), builds, file-existence checks

  api        one commit's changed files + patches, over the host's API
             used for: commit summaries, "what changed"                         cost: calls (5 000/hour)
             rule: summaries need diffs · drafts need files

AI analysis — the job, and what it produced#

Text
  AI — analysis over history                                  model qwen2.5-3b · local · offline
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Job    18 of 24 commits summarised · 6 remaining      [ Run ]  [ Pause ]  [ Run the rest ]
         T3000Webview @ main · since 2026-09-01 · skipped 1 (patch too large: 1.4 MB)

  SUMMARISED
    411c5e55  2 days ago   docs   Clean the docs and move them into the platform repository
                           → moved 3 chapters, rewrote the design hub intro
    f27cf000  5 days ago   docs   Update the docs to add a YAML file for DocFX
                           → affected t3000/architecture (2 pages)

  DRAFTS TO REVIEW
    t3000/architecture/overview.md   +12 −4   "the registry now declares a YAML file…"  [ Open diff ]
    t3000/data-points/README.md      +3  −0   "the Design Studio section moved"         [ Open diff ]

  PAGES OWED   14 pages · oldest 8 months      [ Open the owed list ]

  Nothing here is published or committed: applying a draft is a diff you accept, one `Ctrl+Z` away.

Which page reads what#

Text
  Documents page   ← documents · pages · builds · artifacts · events
  Sources page     ← sources · scans · pages · commits
  Document page    ← doc_sources · recipes · builds · artifacts · pages · commits
  Create a doc     ← sources (what exists)   → documents · doc_sources · recipes
  AI analysis      ← commits · commit_pages · pages   → summaries · drafts · owed
  Build log        ← builds · artifacts
  Notifications    ← events where seen_at is null

What every surface obeys#

  • Say where the facts came from. Every row carries its fidelity — local, fetch or api · floor.
  • Empty states act. A page with nothing on it offers the one thing that applies, never a sentence telling the reader to go and find it.
  • A problem lands where the fix is — the page for a page problem, its row for a document that has never been built.
  • Nothing is written to a source, and nothing is published, except by a command the user ran and confirmed.

Decisions#

Decision Made
The AI's dock docked on the right by the workbench — the secondary side bar takes any view and remembers the position. No contribution point can place it there, so a fresh install needs one drag, and that drag is the documented setup step
The catalog's store node:sqlite — built into the Node the extension host runs, so the platform adds no dependency for it. Where that built-in is missing, the store refuses in words at the point of use and activation is unaffected
Branch policy the default branch, with the mismatch reported and a per-source override
Notification default docs-only — a daily summary of documentation change, no modals
The entry point the welcome page opens on activation (temcoWorkbench.start.open, default welcome, with the checkbox in its own footer as VS Code has it), falling through to the project's pages, then the page you were last on, then the overview. The one recorded project selects itself, so the tree is ready without anyone picking it
The Workspace, gated by content the Workspace stays the first view and the Library sits beneath it, and the open folders are never read into it. Its empty states are rows the tree draws itself, offering the act that fills it — create a project · choose one in the Library · open this project and read its sources. Hiding the view on a context key (when:) and phrasing these states as viewsWelcome were both tried and rejected: a selected project with no visible tree reads as a fault, and a welcome's when is resolved before the refresh has read anything

Build order#

Step What Done when
R1 The catalog — the store, its schema, migrations, and the rows above done: 12 tables, applied idempotently and exercised against a real node:sqlite database — inserts, the document↔source join, the unseen-events query. The store lives in globalStorageUri, never in a repository
R2 Sources — add a git source (any host, chosen branch) or a folder; local, materialised and online modes partly built: a source is added, read in local and api mode, and remembered across restarts. Not built: the materialised (fetch) mode, and the branch mismatch is reported by the Content view rather than by a read
R3 Documents — create one, cite sources, choose a recipe, and build it partly built: a project is created, cites sources, chooses a recipe, and its build runs the repository's own script as a task and records the files by path. Not verified: a real artifact (t3000_dev.chm) has not been produced through this path yet
R4 AI over history — commit summaries, affected pages, drafts, the owed list, as a resumable job a real commit has a summary and a draft, and a human still approves
R5 The views — Documents and Sources: health, fidelity, latest push, Since you last looked partly built: the sidebar holds Workspace (the pages of the project being worked on, with a row saying why while there is nothing) first and Library (projects · sources · repositories · catalog · needs attention · the AI) beneath it, and What needs doing answers "what do I have, and what changed?" on a page. Not built: the Since you last looked digest, and fidelity per source beyond the read mode
R6 Editing and publishing — the editor with its toolbar, creating a document, images, draft branches, the design package's hosted editor, PR flow partly built: the toolbar is built on VS Code's own editor — emphasis, blocks, a link to a real page, the outline — as the sixteen temcoDocs.format.* commands in src/format.ts. A page can be created, named, moved and retired — src/pageOps.ts, six commands and a drag controller — and a project's own scripts can be run from its card on the projects page. Not built: inserting an image, drafts and the PR flow, which need the fetch read mode and a review flow that lives in the product repository

R6 is mostly a rule change, and the rule was changed by naming it. The toolbar edits the buffer a person is already typing in, so it adds no writer at all. Creating a page writes one file — the repository's own docs:registry adds the entry, derives its place from the path and its title from the first heading, so nothing here writes an entry for a page that did not exist. And a page that is moved changes one curated value at a time in docs/help/registry.json, through src/registryEdit.ts, which renders the file the way its own generator does — including the file's line endings — so a move is a two-line diff. docs/editor-design.md §5 records the decision, the four rules that hold it, and the evidence.

R1–R3 make it a documentation platform: sources in, documents and artifacts out. R4 makes it intelligent. R5 makes it a management system. R6 closes the loop.

What this does not change#

  • Content never moves. A document cites sources; it never relocates their pages.
  • Only artifacts ship. A customer installation receives the CHM and the F1 map — never this app.
  • The AI proposes; a person approves.
  • The design package still wins on content, registry and publishing rules. This document only says what the platform knows, where it keeps it, and what it builds.

ui/redesign.title: Docs center: the redesign
ui/redesign.html:
One consolidated design for the documentation center. It supersedes the layout sections of app-flow.md, authoring-flow.md and extension-design.md, which contradict each other. Nothing here is built yet.

1. The model#

Text
 Sources ─► Temco Platform (authoring) ─► Product package ─► Temco Learn (website)
 repos, pdf,   projects · AI · review       products/<id>/       search · downloads · versions
 word, chm                                  manifest.json
                                            docs/ api/ guides/ assets/ releases/
System Job Where
Temco Platform where people work: projects, sources, AI drafts, review, generate this repository
Product package the unit of exchange; a plug-in the portal discovers products/<id>/
Temco Learn the reader's MSDN-style portal the temco-learn repository
DocFX one pluggable build engine; CHM and PDF are other exporters invoked by Build, never a surface

Vocabulary. Project (a documents row) → Section (the registry's area) → Folder (its chapter, nestable) → Page. Versions come from the project's releases. A products table is added only if several versions must be open at once.

Truth rule. Markdown and registry.json in the repository are the content. catalog.sqlite is a register (projects, sources, builds, releases, drafts, caches) and never holds a second copy of page text, except a draft not yet accepted.

2. Journey#

Text
 A LAUNCH ─► B START PAGE ─► C CREATE PROJECT ─► D EMPTY PROJECT ─► E ADD PAGES
                                                                        │
   I RELEASE ◄─ H PUBLISH ◄─ G NEEDS YOU / AI LOOP ◄─ F EDIT / CAPTURE ◄┘

A. First launch#

Text
┌────┬───────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ▤◀ │ DOCS                      │  Welcome to Temco Docs                                       │
│    │  No project yet           │   ┌─ Start ─────────────────┐  ┌─ Bring in existing ───────┐ │
│    │  [ ＋ Create a project ]  │   │ ＋ New project          │  │ Word · RTF · CHM · HTML   │ │
│    │  [ ⇩ Import a doc set  ]  │   │ ▤ From a template       │  │ A folder of Markdown      │ │
│    │  [ ⎇ Open a repository ]  │   │ ⎇ From a repository     │  │ A git repository          │ │
│    │                           │   └─────────────────────────┘  └───────────────────────────┘ │
├────┴───────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ catalog.sqlite created · default organisation written                                         │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

B. Start page (projects exist; shown in the editor, not a container)#

Text
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Temco Docs                                                      ＋ New project │
│ RECENT PROJECTS                                                               │
│  ▤ T3000 Documentation   v13.0   3 sources   built 12:04 ✓   [ Open ] [ ⋯ ]   │
│  ▤ BACnet Tools          v1.2    1 source    never built     [ Open ] [ ⋯ ]   │
│ NEEDS YOU (all projects)                 RECENT ACTIVITY                      │
│  ⚑ 2 drafts waiting       T3000          12:04 build site ✓ T3000             │
│  📷 1 screenshot to place  T3000          11:40 capture placed → Scaling       │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

C. Create a project (4 steps)#

Text
 1 ORIGIN   ◉ Blank · ○ From a template · ○ From a repository · ○ Import a document set · ○ Open existing
 2 BASICS   Name [T3000 Documentation]  Version [13.0]  Owner [alice ▾]  Audience [developer ▾]
 3 SOURCES  ☑ ⎇ t3000webview [main ▾] [src/**]   ☑ ⎇ t3000-esp [main ▾]   ＋ GitHub org · folder · archive
 4 OUTPUTS  Engine [DocFX ▾]  ☑ Website ☑ PDF ☑ CHM ☑ Search index ☐ AI index  →  Review  →  [ Create ]

Create writes documents, doc_sources, recipes and the smallest valid docs/help/registry.json. The six default sections are seeded for a blank project: Overview, Guides, Architecture, API, Troubleshooting, Release Notes.

D. First open (empty project)#

Text
┌────┬───────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ▤◀ │ DOCS                ＋ 🗀 ⟳│ T3000 Documentation 13.0                                 │
│    │ ▾ T3000 Docs · 13.0       │  Your project is ready. Next:                            │
│    │     (empty)               │   ① Add the first page            [ New Page ]           │
│    │ ▸ NEEDS YOU          (0)  │   ② Bring in existing material     [ Import ]            │
│    │ ▸ SOURCES            (2)  │   ③ Let the AI draft from sources  [ Draft sections ]    │
│    │ ▸ PUBLISH                 │                                                          │
└────┴───────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

3. The window#

Text
┌────┬─────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┐
│ ▤◀ │ DOCS                  ＋ 🗀 ⟳│ first-project.md × │ Preview │ ASSIST                   │
│    │ ▾ T3000 Docs · 13.0  (pick) │                              │ [Draft][Properties]      │
│    │   ▾ Overview            3   │ markdown editor              │  title · owner · ship    │
│    │   ▾ Guides             14   │  Ctrl+Alt+S inserts image    │  keywords · help ids     │
│    │     ▾ Getting Started   4   │                              │  code · reviewed         │
│    │         First project  ●    │                              │                          │
│    │   ▸ API · Troubleshooting…  │                              │                          │
│    │ ▸ NEEDS YOU (7)  collapsed  │                              │                          │
│    │ ▸ SOURCES (3)    collapsed  │                              │                          │
│    │ ▸ PUBLISH        collapsed  │                              │                          │
├────┴─────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┤
│ T3000 13.0 · 318 pages · 14 stale · 0 problems         ⚑ 2 drafts        site ✓ · help ✗    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Constraints from the VS Code API that shape this layout:

  • A tree view cannot hold dropdowns, so the project is the tree's first row. Clicking it opens a quick-pick; the view title shows it too.
  • The three lower views are independent panes, collapsed by default. There is no accordion behaviour.
  • A text editor has no tabs: Edit and Preview use the Markdown side-by-side preview, and Properties is a tab in the right panel.
  • Dropping on the tree reports only the row dropped on, never the gap between rows.
  • The tree is path-based. A page id is its path under docs/, so guides/getting-started/install.md is the page install in the folder getting-started, inside guides. Every folder level is derived from those paths: the registry does not have to name the middle folders, and folders nest to any depth.

4. E. The Pages tree#

Rows and hover icons#

Text
 PAGES                                            ＋  🗀  ⇩  ⟳  ⋯
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ▾ Guides                                    14                     │
│   ▾ Getting Started                  [＋][🗀][⋯]     ← folder hover │
│       Install                                                      │
│       First project   ●              [📷][✦][⋯]      ← page hover   │
│       Licensing                                                    │
│ ▾ API                                                              │
│   ▾ Data Points API                                                │
│       Scaling         ⚠  📷                                         │
│         └ ⚠ code changed since last review                         │
│         └ 📷 no image on this page                                 │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 Folder row: name and page count only. Leaf row: title only.
 State is a badge (● draft · ⚠ stale · 📷 no image) or a folded child, never an extra row.
 Hover icons: folder = ＋ New Page · 🗀 New Folder · ⋯ ;  page = 📷 Capture · ✦ Draft with AI · ⋯
 Tooltip: id · owner · audience · last change.

New page and new folder: the selection is the location#

Text
 Selected row            New Page lands…            New Folder lands…
 ─────────────────────   ────────────────────────   ──────────────────────
 nothing / empty space   at the root of the section the root
 a folder                inside it                  inside it (a sub-folder)
 a page                  next to it                 next to it
Text
 click ＋ (or Ctrl+N with the tree focused)
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ New page in  Guides / Getting Started                                  │
 │ [ First project________________________ ]                              │
 │   → getting-started/first-project.md                                   │
 │                              Enter = create    Esc = cancel            │
 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
          │ Enter ─► file written, registry entry added, row selected, page opens
Act You type Automatic
New Page title file name from the slug, kind Article, last position, registry entry, empty template
New Page ▸ Task / Reference / Troubleshooting / Release Note title the same, with the kind set
New Folder folder name the folder and its first page, since an empty chapter does not exist in the registry

The input box is a quick-input, the closest thing the extension API allows to Explorer's inline edit. Renaming in the row itself would need a change to the core of this fork and is deferred.

Context menus#

Text
 on a FOLDER row             on a PAGE row                    on empty space
┌─────────────────────┐    ┌───────────────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐
│ New Page…           │    │ Open · Open to the Side   │    │ New Page…       │
│ New Folder…         │    │ ───────────────────────── │    │ New Folder…     │
│ Import Here…        │    │ New Page…  (sibling)      │    │ Import…         │
│ ─────────────────── │    │ New Page of a Kind  ▸     │    │ Refresh         │
│ Rename…       F2    │    │ ───────────────────────── │    └─────────────────┘
│ Move Up / Down      │    │ Rename File…       F2     │
│ ─────────────────── │    │ Rename Title…  Shift+F2   │
│ Reveal · Copy Path  │    │ Move Up / Down            │
│ Delete…             │    │ ───────────────────────── │
└─────────────────────┘    │ Capture…  Ctrl+Alt+S      │
                           │ Paste Image  Ctrl+Alt+V   │
                           │ Draft a Change with AI…   │
                           │ Mark Reviewed             │
                           │ ───────────────────────── │
                           │ Reveal · Copy Path        │
                           │ Delete…                   │
                           └───────────────────────────┘

Keys#

Text
 F2 rename file (old id kept as an alias)    Shift+F2 rename title only    Delete  with confirmation
 Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V  copy or move rows between folders      Enter / click  open the page

F2 moves the file, the repository's own generator writes the new registry entry, and the old id is written into aliases first. A project with no generator is refused, because the rename would orphan inbound links.

Drag and drop#

Text
 drag a page   onto a FOLDER row  → into that folder, last position
               onto a PAGE row    → into that page's folder, right after it
               onto empty space   → to the section root
 multi-select  Ctrl/Shift+click, then drag together          Ctrl+drag  copies
 every move    → file moves, `order` rewritten, old id kept as an alias
 refused       → into itself or its own child; across projects
 from the OS   → a .md, .png or .docx dropped on a folder is imported there

5. F. Editing a page#

Text
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────┐
│ first-project.md        [ side-by-side Preview ]              │ ASSIST           │
│ # First project                                               │ [Draft][Ask][Props]
│ Points carry a scale factor.                                  │ Draft from…      │
│ ![Trend log](media/02-trend.png)  ◄─ Ctrl+Alt+S inserts this  │  ◉ source file   │
│                                                               │  ○ another page  │
│                                                               │ RESULT (diff)    │
│                                                               │ [Apply][Reject]  │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────┘
 Capture: snip overlay → clipboard → media/NN-slug.png (warn < 1600 px, refuse > 2 MB).
 No page in front → .temco/captures/ and a row in NEEDS YOU until it is attached.
 Apply is one undoable edit. Drafts wait in SQLite until accepted.

The Properties tab is the form over the registry fields: title, section, order, owner, audience, ship, keywords, help ids, code, reviewed.

6. G. Needs You and the AI loop#

Text
 NEEDS YOU (7)
  📷 Screenshots to place (1)  row → "which page takes it?"
  ⚠ Retake these (4)          row → the page
  ○ Never reviewed (2)        row → the report
  ● Drafts waiting (2)        row → diff, Apply / Reject

 source changes ─► commit summarised once (model recorded) ─► mapped to pages (code-glob · path · terms)
   ─► page marked stale ─► NEEDS YOU ─► Draft a Change ─► draft row ─► diff ─► Apply

7. H. Publish#

Text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PUBLISH · T3000 Documentation 13.0                                 │
│  ① REVIEW ───► ② BUILD ───► ③ RELEASE                              │
│  2 waiting     site ✓ help ✗   not released                        │
│ ① drafts and changed pages: [Open diff] [Approve]                  │
│ ② Engine [DocFX ▾] ☑Website ☑PDF ☑CHM ☐ZIP   [▶ Build]             │
│    success is the artifact left behind, never the exit code        │
│ ③ Writes products/t3000/releases/13.0, latest → 13.0   [⬆ Release] │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

8. I. Result on disk, and Temco Learn#

Text
 products/t3000/
   manifest.json   {id, title, version}
   docs/ guides/ api/ assets/ toc.yml docfx.json
   releases/13.0 · 12.9 · 12.8      latest → 13.0
                    │
                    ▼
 Temco Learn discovers products/*  →  Home · Product page · Doc page · Downloads (Online · PDF · CHM · ZIP)

The Learn page's top navigation mirrors the project's sections, so what the writer sees in the tree is what the reader sees.

9. SQLite storage (catalog.sqlite)#

Text
 organisations ─┬─< repositories           cache of what GitHub listed
                │
 sources ───────┤  kind git|folder|archive · remote_url · path · branch · registry_path · last_commit
   │            └──< scans
   ├──< commits ──< commit_pages           sha · summary · summary_model · how: code-glob|path|terms
   │ n..n (doc_sources: branch, include_glob, role)
   ▼
 documents  (the PROJECT)  name · slug · version · audience · owner · origin · template
   ├── 1:1 ─ recipes          engine · config_path · script · outputs
   ├──< pages                 id · path · title · owner · reviewed_at · stale · counts   (cache of registry.json)
   ├──< builds ──< artifacts  status · revision · log_path  /  kind · path · bytes · sha256
   ├──< releases              version · destination · files · published_at · build_id
   └──< drafts                page_id · title · body · state draft|accepted|discarded
 events  at · kind · subject · detail · seen_at       meta  key/value schema version

10. What the extension does now#

The rule this table records: one list, one owner. Every kind of list has exactly one surface, and a webview page never lists something a tree or a panel already lists. Everything a webview page did became a command on that surface.

Then Now
views Pages, Project, Pipeline, Working Set, plus the queue declared in temco-workbench Pages, Needs You, Sources, Publish — all declared by temco-docs
3-step New Page wizard the selection is the location; one title box
10 webview pages (projects, project, needs, repository, documents, page, source, review, builds, releases) 2 left: Project home and Release report. The other eight commands still exist and now focus the surface that owns the list, so every button and menu item in the other modules still lands somewhere
the tree stopped at area → chapter → page the tree is a path: folders inside folders, any depth, like Explorer
Working Set removed (use Open Editors)
Properties as an editor panel the right panel's Properties tab, beside Draft
publishing copied artifacts publishing also writes manifest.json per product and regenerates the Learn portal
home.ts, views.ts named in extension-design.md do not exist; that document now points here

11. Where the work stands#

Done:

  1. The three older documents carry a pointer here instead of a competing layout.
  2. The four views, the queue moved out of temco-workbench, Sources/Publish renamed.
  3. The project is the tree's first row; a new project is seeded with the six sections.
  4. New Page and New Folder take their location from the selection; hover icons; multi-select drag and drop.
  5. Properties is a tab in the right panel.
  6. manifest.json is written on publish, and the Learn portal is generated from every product's manifest.

Not done, and deliberately so:

  • The temco-learn site itself. The portal is generated by this extension and served from local storage; a real reader site is a separate repository.
  • Inline rename in the tree row. It needs a change to the fork's tree widget; an input box is the closest the extension API allows.
  • Dropping between rows. The tree reports only the row dropped on, so a drop on a page means "after it".

Open decisions#

  • Whether products becomes a table later (versions open side by side).
  • Whether the six sections stay fixed, or are defined per project in manifest.json.

ui/shell-v2.title: Shell and pages, v2 — the full layout, drawn
ui/shell-v2.html:
This supersedes the shell, activity-bar and left-panel parts of application-design.md. Every surface below is drawn in full; nothing is summarised as "keeps the same frame".

Counted from the manifests before designing anything:

today v2
activity-bar containers 5 4
side-bar views 19 7
center pages ~44 17
commands 250+ 250+ (every id unchanged)

Legend: [ Button ] is a button · ▸ ▾ • are tree disclosure and items · ⋯ is a menu · ⬚ is a picture · ‹ › are tabs · ◀ marks the selected row · (•) marks a radio choice.

The four rules#

  1. A side bar is a list you work in — not a dashboard, not a status board. Status belongs to the status bar; actions belong to the view's title bar.
  2. A row is a thing, or it is an action — never both. test11.md is a thing. Build Center is an action wearing a tree row at the same weight, which is why the column reads as noise.
  3. One name per concept. Not Needs You here and Review Center there. Not Publish for both "copy a build" and "push to GitHub".
  4. A module with nothing to show gets no icon. An empty container is a broken promise.

1. The window#

Text
┌────┬──────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┬────────────────────┐
│ ⌂  │ [view title]            ⋯  ＋ │                             │ AI                 │
│ ▤  │ [ one-line header / search ]  │      the page you are       │ ─────────────────  │
│ ⌗  │ ────────────────────────────  │      working in             │ you: …             │
│ ≡  │                              │                             │ ai: …              │
│    │     the list you work in     │  ┌───────────────────────┐  ├────────────────────┤
│    │                              │  │                       │  │ PAGE               │
│    │                              │  │                       │  │ Outline·Draft·Props│
├────┴──────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┴────────────────────┤
│ PROBLEMS · OUTPUT · TERMINAL                                                          │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ▤ Test1 · 148 pages · 1 owed · v1.4 · Build ✓ 10:42 · Pages ✓                          │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Left one container, one list · Center one page · Right two secondary side bars that follow the page (§5) · Bottom the window's facts, once.

2. Activity bar: four icons#

The activity bar is the whole application's top-level navigation: one icon is one container, and a container is one side bar. That is the only structure VS Code gives an extension, so the bar is where "how many places does this application have?" is decided.

Text
 ┌────┬──────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │    │ GLYPH        │ TOOLTIP — what the icon is                               │
 ├────┼──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │  1 │ house        │ Home — projects, recent activity, repositories, the site   │
 │  2 │ book         │ Docs — the documentation workspace                        │
 │  3 │ grid         │ Tools — SQL, BACnet, IO, network                          │
 │  4 │ sliders      │ Settings — settings and help                              │
 ├────┼──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 │  5 │ account      │ accounts                     (VS Code's own, not ours)    │
 │  6 │ gear         │ Manage                       (VS Code's own, not ours)    │
 └────┴──────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Rows 1–4 are ours; 5–6 belong to VS Code and cannot be removed. The whole bar can be collapsed by the user at any time, so nothing here may be the only way to reach a page — every icon's contents are also in the command palette.

2.1 What each icon opens#

# icon tooltip side bar it opens the job it does you reach for it when
1 house Home Projects · Repositories · Recent activity orient: which project, which Temco code the docs are written from, what happened, what was published you start a session, or you are not sure what to do next
2 book Docs Pages write: the tree of pages, the two acts that ship them you are working on the documentation, which is most of the time
3 grid Tools Query & Browse · Schema & Maintenance diagnose: devices, IO points, BACnet objects, network, SQL a controller is misbehaving, or you need data out of the system
4 sliders Settings Settings configure: appearance, modules, models, publishing, help something is wrong with the installation, or you are changing how it behaves

The lists are unevenly split — Home 3, Docs 1, Tools 2, Settings 1 — because that is the real number of lists that hold things you click into (rule 1). An uneven bar is the honest bar: a container with one list is fine, a container kept only so the bar looks symmetric is not.

2.2 Why these four, in this order#

Text
   orient ──▶ write ──▶ diagnose ──▶ configure
     ⌂          ▤           ⌗            ≡
   (daily)   (all day)    (sometimes)  (rarely)
  • Order follows a session, not a feature list. Left to right is the order a person actually moves: find the project, do the work, investigate a problem, change a setting. Icons are muscle memory; the position is the documentation.
  • One icon per kind of activity, not per module. Nine modules, four activities: that is why the count is four and not nine, and why adding a module does not add an icon.
  • The test for membership. An icon earns its place only if it opens a list you work in and revisit regularly. If it opens one page you visit monthly, it is a row somewhere, not an icon. That test is what removed Learn (read-only output → a page under Home) and AI (see §2.4).

2.3 The Settings glyph: sliders, not a gear#

Text
   ours                          VS Code's
 ┌──────────────┐              ┌──────────────┐
 │   ══╪══      │  sliders     │      ⚙       │  Manage
 │   ══╪══      │              │              │
 └──────────────┘              └──────────────┘
      row 4                        row 6

A gear at 16 px is a grey blob; two gears in one column is one meaning too many, and the one at the bottom is not ours. So the Settings container is drawn as sliders — the second universal conventions for preferences — and its tooltip reads Settings where VS Code's reads Manage.

The container id stays temcoSettings, so saved layout and onView activation are untouched. The whole change is one file: media/settings.svg.

2.4 What is deliberately not in the bar#

not here where it is why
AI the right-hand secondary side bar (§4.16) a conversation is not a destination; it is a thing you have while writing. Putting it on the left would make it a place you leave the page to visit
Published site / Learn Home ▸ Published site (§4.6) read-only output of work done elsewhere — a page, not a place to keep open
Repositories the Home side bar (§4.4) it is the shelf of Temco code that pages are written from — a list of things, opened while orienting, not an activity of its own. The drafting that reads it happens in Docs (§4.8a), and every draft names the file it was given
BACnet · network · device manager inside Tools they are jobs inside the diagnostic activity, not activities of their own — and two of them have no manifest yet, so they must not get an icon that opens nothing (rule 4)

2.5 Before and after#

Today the manifest declares five activity-bar containers, all from temco-workbench:

Text
        TODAY (manifest)                        V2
┌────┐  ⌂ Home        (5 views) ───────▶  ┌────┐  ⌂ Home      (3 views)
│ ⌂  │  ▤ Docs        (6 views) ───────▶  │ ⌂  │  ▤ Docs      (1 view)
│ ▤  │  ✦ AI          (2 views) ───────▶  │ ▤  │  ⌗ Tools     (2 views)
│ ✦  │  ⌗ Tools       (2 views) ───────▶  │ ⌗  │  ≡ Settings  (1 view)
│ ⌗  │  ≡ Settings    (4 views)           │ ≡  │
│ ≡  │                                   └────┘
└────┘
  5 icons · 19 views                     4 icons · 7 views

Two things move — nothing disappears:

  • AI leaves the bar for the right-hand side bar: the assistant and runtime views regroup there (§4.16), next to the draft panel that is already on that side.
  • Repositories changes container. It is a view inside Docs today (the sixth one), which is why it never had an icon. It moves to Home, where "what can I read?" is one of the questions Home answers. Home's five sections today are mostly status boards; under this design it has three real lists — Projects, Repositories, Recent activity — while Docs drops to the single Pages tree (§4.4).

Home, Docs, Tools and Settings all stay. Their contents change (§3–§7), not their identity.

Two other containers exist today but were never in the bar, and this design keeps them out:

container location what it is
temcoAi secondary side bar (right) the AI side bar — already where §2.4 wants AI
temcoDraft auxiliary bar (right, bottom) the AI draft panel, titled Page — it renders the page being written beside the page list

What the eight icons you saw were. The earlier build also carried temcoLearn, temcoHelp and temco-repositories containers. Those three were removed in the manifest fix that preceded this document, which is why the bar reads five today: Learn → Home ▸ Published site, Help → Settings ▸ Help, Repositories → Home ▸ Repositories. So the sequence is 8 → 5 (done, manifest) → 4 (this document, AI leaves).

2.6 States#

Text
   selected              hover                 no project yet
 ┌────┐               ┌────┐                ┌────┐
 │ ▤  │ ◀ accent bar  │ ▤  │ ◀ tint         │ ⌂  │ ◀ Home is where the
 │    │               │    │                │    │   answer is
 └────┘               └────┘                └────┘
  • Selected — the icon for the open container carries VS Code's accent bar; clicking it again collapses the side bar.
  • No badge on any icon. Counts belong to the status bar and to the view that owns them; a number on an icon is read as "notifications" and gets ignored after a week.
  • No empty container, ever (rule 4): if a module has nothing to show it is not in the bar at all.

2.7 What implementing this touches#

change risk
5 containers → 4 (remove the AI container) one manifest, no code — onView for its views moves with them
19 views → 7 views are removed only after their content exists elsewhere (§8); Repositories is moved, not removed
media/settings.svg redrawn as sliders one icon file
container ids unchanged saved layout, onView activation and every when: view == … clause keep working
check-temco-modules already refuses a view inside a container that does not exist a half-finished step fails the build instead of showing an empty panel

The word on the row is repository; inside a project the same thing is called a source (§4.7), because that is what it is there — one of the places a project cites. One entity, two scopes, and the list is the scope where you act on it.

button what it does what it costs
[ Read ] finds docs/*/registry.json inside it — or converts a folder once — and records the pages it holds one API call, or one folder walk; nothing is ever written to the source
[ Draft ] opens the file ticker (§4.5) so code files can be ticked as material for a new page (§4.8a) nothing until Draft is pressed; a page exists only when the draft is accepted

[ Draft ] is the button that makes this page part of writing rather than a library: the code in these repositories is the raw material of every page that is not already written, and the material a page was given is recorded on the page.

Why both a view and a page. The view in the Home side bar is the everyday list — arrow keys, filter, open one. This page is the same sources drawn wide, for what a tree row cannot hold: the organisation they came from, [ + Add a Repository… ], in bulk. One law on both: a row is a thing, an action is in its buttons or ⋯ (rule 2).
